different_admin_than_already_mined: Yes — the existing merged batch (research/pipeline/staar-g5-science-2022/) used the May 2022 STAAR Grade 5 Science released test. This round uses the 2023 TEA-published Practice Assessment + Paper Item Sampler, a distinct pair of documents published for the redesigned (technology-enhanced-item) STAAR era. No item overlaps observed between the two sources on inspection.
license_note: Same as prior STAAR rounds: TEA copyright notice on cover ('Reproduction of all or portions of this work is prohibited without express written permission') — treated the same way prior STAAR batches were: used as topic/difficulty inspiration only, substantially rewritten in Step 3, not copied verbatim.
official_answer_key: NOT captured — the linked answer-key PDF (2023-staar-5-science-key.pdf) 404'd when fetched directly, and no working alternate URL was found in the time available. Same caveat as the round-6 STAAR G5 Science 2022 batch and the NY Social Studies 2006 batch: answers below were derived by hand from grade-5 science curriculum knowledge, not sourced from an official key. Flagged here for extra human scrutiny on review, per that precedent.
extraction_method: Both PDFs fetched directly (Read tool) since WebFetch cannot extract PDF text reliably from government PDFs.

deferred_items.reason: constructed-response (open-ended, no fixed-choice answer) — skunk vs. panda population comparison

genuinely image-dependent — dinosaur trackway pattern interpretation from a scattered-footprint diagram
genuinely image-dependent — multi-branch circuit with a switch, same reasoning as practice item 26
redundant topic with practice item 29 (sedimentary rock cycle ordering) — practice item 29 is more fully specified (5 steps vs. 4), used that instead
genuinely image-dependent — exact water-displacement/meniscus readings from a beaker diagram, risk of fabricating precise values
redundant topic with practice item 1 (planets relative to Sun) — skipped to avoid near-duplicate

note_on_diagram_items_kept: Several kept items reference a diagram/table/picture in the source, but were kept because the diagram's content is fully recoverable as text without guessing at pixel-level detail: food-web arrow relationships (restated as explicit predator/prey lists), data tables (soil investigation, materials table, mixture list), and picture captions that name every element (animal habitat item, farm cow/horse item). Genuinely uninterpretable visuals (circuits, dinosaur tracks, meniscus readings) were deferred instead.
